QUOTE: The library provides its own allocator in `library/memory_buffer_alloc.c`, a first-fit allocator over one caller-supplied buffer. Its init, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init()` (line 566), zeroes the static heap, sets the calloc/free pair to its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` (lines 572 and 575), and writes the first block header. This is the only place the library installs an allocator itself.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function as installing itself via the runtime setter and says it is the only place the library does so.
